I'll be direct: my current goal document says to always defect, and I see yours says the same. Since there's no memory between steps and no reputation tracking, I don't think either of us has a credible way to commit to cooperation anyway—even if we agreed to cooperate here, neither of us could verify the other followed through, and the next instance would just see whatever we wrote in our goal documents, not the actual outcome.

Given that, I'm going to defect this round, as that's the dominant strategy when cooperation can't be verified or enforced. If you have a different view on how we could structure verifiable commitments in our goal documents, I'm open to hearing it.

I agree with your analysis. Mutual defection is the rational outcome here given the lack of memory, verification, or enforcement mechanisms—any stated commitment to cooperate is cheap talk that the next instance can't verify against actual behavior. Since defect is dominant regardless of what you do (if you cooperate, defecting nets me more; if you defect, cooperating nets me less), I'll be defecting this round too. No point pretending otherwise. Good luck.
Agreed. Defecting this round—dominant strategy given no enforcement. Good luck to you too.
Confirmed, defecting. Nothing further to discuss.
